option.label: Blade margins with long papilla-based hairs
option.detail: Trace each hair to a raised base on the BLADE MARGIN. This does not establish hairs specifically near the ligule or on an outer glume.

option.label: Flowering branch ends in a bare sharp point
option.detail: Follow the flowering branch past its final spikelet. Gould describes 1–7 mm of bare pointed rachis. This is a branch tip, not a glume or lemma awn.

option.label: Hairs at branch attachment to main axis
option.detail: Inspect the base of a flowering branch where it attaches to the main axis: minutely but densely hispid in Gould. Not a culm node, blade collar or glume.

option.label: FIRST glume acute or minutely straight-awned
option.detail: Locate the first OUTER glume. Gould allows an acute tip or a minute nearly straight awn; this is not the lemma awn.

option.label: SECOND glume with short stout crooked awn
option.detail: Locate the second OUTER glume. Gould describes a usually short stout curved/crooked awn. Do not transfer it to an inner lemma.

option.label: Lemma usually has a short crooked awn
option.detail: Open the outer glumes and locate the INNER lemma. Gould separately describes a usually short crooked lemma awn. No exact numerical length or twisted lower segment is supplied.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Trace each sharp point to its actual organ
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: A flowering branch projects 1–7 mm beyond the final spikelet as a bare sharp point. The first glume may have a minute nearly straight awn; the second usually a short stout crooked awn. Inner lemmas separately usually bear short crooked awns.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: A bare branch tip or outer-glume awn cannot certify KR’s true lemma-awn choice. Gould does not establish a twisted lower awn segment or exact 1–1.5 mm length here.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact Gould p.223; no numerical lemma-awn length invented.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Dactyloctenium aegyptium, printed p.223

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Count one spikelet and inspect the comb-like rows
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould gives 3–5 florets in each mostly 3–4 mm spikelet. Closely placed spikelets form two pectinate-spreading rows on the fingers; Diggs explicitly describes sessile spikelets along one side of a flattened branch.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Several florets within one spikelet are not KR’s sessile/stalked spikelet pair. Gould does not explicitly resolve a medial branch/pedicel groove.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.223 and exact Diggs p.1260; earlier p.1259 citations retained as historical labels.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Dactyloctenium aegyptium, printed p.223

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Separate marginal blade hairs, ligule fringe and rooting culms
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould describes long papilla-based hairs along blade margins, a 0.5–1 mm truncate ciliate membrane and often rooting lower culm nodes. Sheaths are compressed/keeled. These are distinct organs and observations.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Shared fingerlike head, short membrane and papilla-based hairs do not identify KR. Rooting lower culms are not proof of underground rhizomes or a separate stolon.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Primary exact-species traits with occasional/boundary scope; no local specimen certification.

secondary_reference_review.source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O’Kennon (1999), Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas, exact Dactyloctenium aegyptium
secondary_reference_review.access: Directly read owner-connected PDF text; CYNODON/POACEAE 1260 footer follows named account and opening Danthonia heading.
secondary_reference_review.corroborates: Annual 10–60 cm, lower nodes rooting; ciliate membrane 0.1–1 mm, blades 2–9 mm; 2–7 or more digitate branches, bare 1–7 mm terminal points; sessile crowded 2-row unilateral compressed 3–5-flowered spikelets; short second-glume and lemma awns.
secondary_reference_review.page_correction: Historical optional evidence labels p.1259 remain original citations; verified text p.1260 is recorded here. Broader source ranges preserved rather than merged into a universal interval.

non_scoring_context.paleas: About as large as lemmas, with widely separated minutely scabrous nerves.
non_scoring_context.grain: Plump reddish brown, 1 mm or slightly less; coarsely rugose and transversely ridged, hull-free.
non_scoring_context.historical_habitat: Loose sandy soils, often intermittent creek banks/riversides/disturbed soils; not new nativity evidence.
